summary: This informational document is a roadmap to RFCs relating to TCP. It briefly summarizes the documents defining TCP and its extensions, as a guide for implementers and others.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7414 organizes the documents that describe TCP and its extensions. It shows which RFCs cover core behavior, recommended improvements, experiments, and older ideas, but readers must consult those RFCs for requirements.

questions: what are the core tcp rfcs
subtitle: A guide to the RFCs that define, extend, and discuss TCP.

tldr.problem: TCP's specifications are spread across many RFCs with different roles, making it difficult to know which documents describe core behavior or optional extensions.
tldr.mechanism: The roadmap groups documents into core functionality, encouraged enhancements, experiments, historic or undeployed extensions, and supporting material.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7414 is Informational, obsoletes RFC 4614, and was updated by RFC 7805. It is a descriptive roadmap, not an implementation standard.

sections.title: How to Read the Roadmap
sections.content:
RFC 7414 is a guide to TCP-related RFCs for implementers and readers. It groups documents by their role and adds a letter for each RFC category: Standards Track, Experimental, Informational, Historic, Best Current Practice, or Unknown.

The roadmap says its categories are not definitive and do not determine whether a document is relevant. Its three main groups roughly resemble MUST, SHOULD, and MAY levels, but the roadmap is descriptive and does not create binding requirements. It obsoletes RFC 4614.
sections.plainLanguage: The roadmap helps readers find TCP documents by topic and status. It does not replace those documents or decide what an implementation must support.

sections.title: Documents for Core TCP Behavior
sections.content:
The core group covers TCP header parsing, its state machine, congestion control, and retransmission timeout calculation. RFC 793 is the fundamental specification. RFC 1122 clarifies requirements for Internet hosts, while other listed RFCs address IPv6 checksum processing, urgent indications, congestion control, retransmission timing, and the Maximum Segment Size option.

The roadmap notes that RFC 793 does not describe congestion control. RFC 5681 describes slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery. RFC 6298 updates the initial retransmission timeout from 3 seconds to 1 second.
sections.plainLanguage: Several RFCs together describe the basic rules that let TCP endpoints communicate. Other documents fill in important behavior such as congestion control and retransmission timing.

sections.title: Strongly Encouraged Enhancements
sections.content:
The roadmap lists enhancements that are not part of its required core group but can improve performance or security. Topics include window scaling and timestamps, congestion control, loss recovery, detecting spurious retransmissions, Path MTU Discovery, header compression, and protection against spoofing or flooding.

Examples include selective acknowledgment, NewReno, the TCP Authentication Option, and sequence-number protections. The roadmap describes some as recommended or commonly found, but says implementers should consult each specification for its actual requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: Additional RFCs describe ways to improve throughput, recover from loss, or resist attacks. The roadmap summarizes them, but the individual RFCs contain the detailed rules.

sections.title: Experimental Extensions
sections.content:
The experimental section includes extensions published to gain experience or proposals not widely deployed at the time. The roadmap encourages testing but says wide deployment should be considered carefully because formal agreement on the behavior may not exist.

Examples include TCP Fast Open, which allows data in SYN and SYN-ACK packets, an increased initial window proposal, and Multipath TCP. Experiments that need a TCP option code point are directed to the experimental-use procedures described by RFC 6994.
sections.plainLanguage: Experimental RFCs describe ideas that still need experience or broader agreement. The roadmap asks readers to consider the effects before deploying them widely.

sections.title: Historic Work and Other References
sections.content:
The roadmap groups some older extensions as historic or undeployed because they were defective or did not gain broad use. Examples include the TCP Big Window and Nak options, T/TCP, and TCP Cookie Transactions. It also lists foundational work, architecture guidance, advice for difficult networks, implementation notes, tools, MIB modules, case studies, and undocumented implementation techniques.

The RFC says it introduces no new security considerations. Its contents are a snapshot organized in publication order, and the document cautions that its summaries should not be the sole basis for implementation decisions.
sections.plainLanguage: The roadmap also points to older proposals, guidance, tools, and management documents. Its summaries provide context, while the original RFCs remain the source for technical details.
